import XCTest

class ScreenshotBaseUITestCase: XCTestCase {
    let supportedScreenshotLanguages = ["en", "de", "ja", "fr", "es", "zh-Hans", "nl", "da", "it", "fi"]

    let baseLaunchArguments = [
        "-ui-testing",
        "-ui-reset-userdefaults",
        "-ui-disable-location-tracking",
        "-ui-screenshot-mode"
    ]

    let app = XCUIApplication()

    override func setUpWithError() throws {
        continueAfterFailure = false
    }

    @discardableResult
    @MainActor
    func launchApp(onboardingCompleted: Bool, initialTab: Int? = nil, scenarioID: String) -> XCUIApplication {
        var args = baseLaunchArguments + ["-ui-screenshot-scenario", scenarioID]
        let languageCode = screenshotLanguageCode()
        let regionCode = screenshotRegionCode()
        args += [
            "-AppleLanguages", "(\(appleLanguageIdentifier(for: languageCode)))",
            "-AppleLocale", appleLocaleIdentifier(languageCode: languageCode, regionCode: regionCode)
        ]

        if onboardingCompleted {
            args.append("-ui-onboarding-completed")
        } else {
            args.append("-ui-show-onboarding")
        }

        if let initialTab {
            args += ["-ui-initial-tab", String(initialTab)]
        }

        app.launchArguments = args
        app.launchEnvironment["SCREENSHOT_LANG"] = languageCode
        app.launchEnvironment["SCREENSHOT_REGION"] = regionCode
        app.launchEnvironment["SCREENSHOT_DEVICE_NAME"] = screenshotDeviceName()
        app.launch()
        return app
    }

    @MainActor
    func captureScenarioScreenshot(index: Int, slug: String) {
        let attachment = XCTAttachment(screenshot: XCUIScreen.main.screenshot())
        attachment.lifetime = .keepAlways
        attachment.name = screenshotFileName(index: index, slug: slug)
        add(attachment)
    }

    func screenshotLanguageCode() -> String {
        let envLang = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["SCREENSHOT_LANG"]
        if let envLang, !envLang.isEmpty, let normalized = normalizeLanguageCode(envLang) {
            return normalized
        }

        if let appleLanguage = languageFromAppleLanguageSettings() {

    var deviceID: String {
        if let cached = cachedDeviceID {
            return cached
        }
        // Safely attempt to load the persisted ID; fall back to generating
        // and storing a new one if loading fails for any reason.
        guard let loaded = loadDeviceID() else {
            // Fallback: create a fresh ID to avoid crashes on startup
            let newID = UUID().uuidString
            saveDeviceID(newID)
            cachedDeviceID = newID
            return newID
        }
        cachedDeviceID = loaded
        return loaded
    }

    /// Persists and activates a specific deviceID value for this app install.
    func setDeviceID(_ id: String) {
        let trimmed = id.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
        guard !trimmed.isEmpty else {
            debugLog("[DEBUG] Ignoring empty deviceID set request.")
            return
        }
        let oldID = cachedDeviceID
        saveDeviceID(trimmed)
        cachedDeviceID = trimmed
        if oldID?.uppercased() != trimmed.uppercased() {
            DispatchQueue.main.async {
                NotificationCenter.default.post(
                    name: .thisDeviceIDDidChange,
                    object: nil,
                    userInfo: [
                        "oldDeviceID": oldID ?? "",
                        "newDeviceID": trimmed
                    ]
                )
            }
        }
    }

    /// Generates, persists and activates a brand new deviceID.

extension UserDefaults {
    var hasCompletedOnboarding: Bool {
        get { bool(forKey: "hasCompletedOnboarding") }
        set { set(newValue, forKey: "hasCompletedOnboarding") }
    }

    var hasShownPostUpdateOnboarding: Bool {
        get { bool(forKey: "hasShownPostUpdateOnboarding") }
        set { set(newValue, forKey: "hasShownPostUpdateOnboarding") }
    }

    var hadLocationTrackingEnabled: Bool {
        bool(forKey: "track_and_report_location")
    }
}

class AppState: ObservableObject {
    @Published var showOnboarding: Bool
    @Published var onboardingMode: OnboardingMode

    init() {
        let defaults = UserDefaults.standard
        if !defaults.hasCompletedOnboarding {
            onboardingMode = .full
            showOnboarding = true
            return
        }

        if !defaults.hasShownPostUpdateOnboarding, defaults.hadLocationTrackingEnabled {
            onboardingMode = .postUpdate
            showOnboarding = true
            return
        }

        onboardingMode = .full
        showOnboarding = false
    }

    func presentFullOnboarding(skipPostUpdate: Bool) {
        if skipPostUpdate {
            UserDefaults.standard.hasShownPostUpdateOnboarding = true
        }
        onboardingMode = .full
        showOnboarding = true
    }
}

    static let shared = RotationLockController()

    private var isRotationLocked = false
    private var lockedOrientationMask: UIInterfaceOrientationMask = .portrait

        guard isRotationLocked else { return .all }
        return lockedOrientationMask
    }

    func setRotationLockEnabled(_ enabled: Bool) {
        if !Thread.isMainThread {

                self?.setRotationLockEnabled(enabled)
            }

        }

        isRotationLocked = enabled
        if enabled {
            lockedOrientationMask = currentInterfaceOrientationMask()
        }

        let targetMask = isRotationLocked ? lockedOrientationMask : .all
        let scenes = UIApplication.shared.connectedScenes.compactMap { $0 as? UIWindowScene }

        for scene in scenes {
            scene.windows.forEach { $0.rootViewController?.setNeedsUpdateOfSupportedInterfaceOrientations() }
            if #available(iOS 16.0, *) {

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-05-26 08:35:23Z)**_

This is happening because the UI/screenshot tests deliberately wipe `UserDefaults` at app launch.

The key path is:

- [ExtendedUITests.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataruUITests/ExtendedUITests.swift:4) launches with `-ui-reset-userdefaults`.
- [ScreenshotBaseUITestCase.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataruScreenshotUITests/ScreenshotBaseUITestCase.swift:6) does the same.
- [miataruApp.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/miataruApp.swift:443) handles that flag by calling `removePersistentDomain(forName:)`, wiping the app’s defaults.
- The local DeviceKey is stored in `UserDefaults` as `device_key`: [SettingsManager.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/SettingsManagers/App%20Settings/SettingsManager.swift:206), [SettingsConfiguration.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/SettingsManagers/App%20Settings/SettingsConfiguration.swift:48).

The subtle part: your `deviceID` is not stored in `UserDefaults`; it is stored as a file in Application Support: [thisDeviceIDManager.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/SettingsManagers/App%20Settings/thisDeviceIDManager.swift:75). So after tests run, the simulator can keep the same server-side device identity, but the local DeviceKey is gone. If that device already has a DeviceKey set on the server, the app now has a device ID whose matching local key was erased, so it looks like the simulator “lost” the DeviceKey and needs recovery/reset.

To avoid it:

1. Use a dedicated simulator for UI/screenshot tests, not your normal development simulator.
2. Do not run UI tests against a real DeviceKey-protected device identity.
3. Best code-side fix: change the UI-test reset to preserve `device_key`, `device_key_last_changed`, and related auth fields when the test launch only needs deterministic onboarding/settings state.
4. Alternative: when `-ui-reset-userdefaults` is used, also regenerate/reset the local `deviceID` so the app does not keep an old server-protected identity with no local key.
5. Longer-term best fix: move DeviceKey storage out of plain `UserDefaults` into Keychain, and make the UI-test reset avoid clearing Keychain unless a separate explicit `-ui-reset-sensitive-data` flag is passed.

Most likely immediate culprit: `-ui-reset-userdefaults` is too broad for a simulator you care about.

  APP_BUILD_OVERRIDE     Override app build number in artifact structure
  ARTIFACT_VERSION_TAG   Explicit artifact version folder name (highest priority)
EOF
}

trim_whitespace() {
  local value="$1"
  value="${value#"${value%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
  value="${value%"${value##*[![:space:]]}"}"
  printf '%s' "$value"
}

sanitize_slug() {
  local input="$1"

  value="$(printf '%s' "$input" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed -E 's/[^a-z0-9_-]+/-/g; s/^-+//; s/-+$//; s/-+/-/g')"
  if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
    value="unknown"
  fi
  printf '%s' "$value"
}

strip_xcresult_attachment_suffix() {
  local value="$1"

  printf '%s' "$value" | sed -E 's/_[0-9]+_[0-9A-Fa-f-]{36}(\.[[:alnum:]]+)$/\1/'
}

method_name_from_test_identifier() {
  local test_identifier="$1"
  local method="${test_identifier##*/}"
  method="${method%%(*}"
  printf '%s' "$method"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"

PROJECT_PATH="${PROJECT_PATH:-$REPO_ROOT/miataru.xcodeproj}"
SCHEME="${SCHEME:-miataru}"
CONFIGURATION="${CONFIGURATION:-Debug}"

resolve_destination() {
  if [[ -n "${TEST_DESTINATION:-}" ]]; then
    echo "$TEST_DESTINATION"
    return
  fi

  local booted
  booted="$(xcrun simctl list devices available | grep -E 'iPhone|iPad' | grep 'Booted' | head -n1 | awk -F '[()]' '{print $2}')"
  if [[ -n "$booted" ]]; then
    echo "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$booted"
    return
  fi

  local first_iphone
  first_iphone="$(xcrun simctl list devices available | grep 'iPhone' | head -n1 | awk -F '[()]' '{print $2}')"
  if [[ -n "$first_iphone" ]]; then
    echo "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$first_iphone"
    return
  fi

  local first_ipad
  first_ipad="$(xcrun simctl list devices available | grep 'iPad' | head -n1 | awk -F '[()]' '{print $2}')"
  if [[ -n "$first_ipad" ]]; then
    echo "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$first_ipad"
    return
  fi

  echo "platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16"
}

run_tests() {
  local only_testing="${1:-}"
  shift || true

  local destination
  destination="$(resolve_destination)"

  local args=(
    -project "$PROJECT_PATH"
    -scheme "$SCHEME"
    -configuration "$CONFIGURATION"
    -destination "$destination"
  )

  if [[ -n "$only_testing" ]]; then
    args+=("-only-testing:$only_testing")
  fi

  if [[ -n "${RESULT_BUNDLE_PATH:-}" ]]; then
    args+=(-resultBundlePath "$RESULT_BUNDLE_PATH")
  fi

  echo "Running xcodebuild test"
  echo "  project: $PROJECT_PATH"
  echo "  scheme: $SCHEME"
  echo "  config: $CONFIGURATION"
  echo "  destination: $destination"
  if [[ -n "$only_testing" ]]; then
    echo "  only-testing: $only_testing"
  fi

  xcodebuild test "${args[@]}" "$@"
}

latest_ios_runtime_id() {

}

find_simulator_udid_by_name() {
  local simulator_name="$1"
  xcrun simctl list devices available | awk -v target="$simulator_name" '
    index($0, target " (") > 0 {
      if (match($0, /[0-9A-F-]{36}/)) {
        print substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH)
        exit
      }
    }
  '
}

ensure_simulator() {
  local simulator_name="$1"
  local device_type_id="$2"

  local existing
  existing="$(find_simulator_udid_by_name "$simulator_name" || true)"
  if [[ -n "$existing" ]]; then
    echo "$existing"
    return
  fi

  local runtime_id
  runtime_id="$(latest_ios_runtime_id)"
  if [[ -z "$runtime_id" ]]; then
    echo "Unable to find available iOS simulator runtime." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "Creating simulator: $simulator_name ($device_type_id, $runtime_id)" >&2
  xcrun simctl create "$simulator_name" "$device_type_id" "$runtime_id" >/dev/null

  local created
  created="$(find_simulator_udid_by_name "$simulator_name" || true)"
  if [[ -z "$created" ]]; then
    echo "Failed to create simulator for $simulator_name" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "$created"
}

_**Agent (gpt-5.5 2026-05-26 08:36:58Z)**_

Set them up by always passing `xcodebuild` a dedicated simulator UDID, never letting it auto-pick a booted simulator.

Your common test runner already supports this through `TEST_DESTINATION`: [miataru/scripts/_test-common.sh](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/scripts/_test-common.sh:11). The risky bit is that without it, it first selects any booted iPhone/iPad simulator: [miataru/scripts/_test-common.sh](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/scripts/_test-common.sh:16).

Example setup:

```bash
RUNTIME="$(xcrun simctl list runtimes available | awk -F ' - ' '/iOS .*com.apple.CoreSimulator.SimRuntime.iOS-/{print $NF}' | tail -n1)"

UDID="$(xcrun simctl create \
  "miataru UI Tests - iPhone 16" \
  "com.apple.CoreSimulator.SimDeviceType.iPhone-16" \
  "$RUNTIME")"

TEST_DESTINATION="platform=iOS Simulator,id=$UDID" \
  ./miataru/scripts/test-ui.sh
```

For repeatable local use, create it once, then reuse its UDID:

```bash
xcrun simctl list devices available | grep "miataru UI Tests"
```

Then run:

```bash
TEST_DESTINATION="platform=iOS Simulator,id=<UDID>" ./miataru/scripts/test-ui.sh
```

Best repo-level setup would be:

1. Add an `ensure_test_simulator` helper to `_test-common.sh`.
2. Make `test-ui.sh` and `test-functional-ui-serial.sh` default to a named simulator like `miataru UI Tests - iPhone 16`.
3. Change screenshot simulator names to be prefixed too, for example `miataru Screenshots - iPhone 16 Pro Max`, because the screenshot script currently looks up plain device names and could collide with your normal simulator.

Optional but useful: erase only the dedicated test simulator before runs:

```bash
xcrun simctl shutdown <UDID> || true
xcrun simctl erase <UDID>
```

That gives tests a clean playground while your normal simulator keeps its DeviceKey and app state untouched.

What changed:

- [miataru/scripts/_test-common.sh](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/scripts/_test-common.sh:10) now defaults to a dedicated simulator named `miataru Tests - iPhone 16`.
- If that simulator does not exist, the script creates it automatically using the latest available iOS runtime.
- `test-ui.sh`, `test-unit.sh`, `test-all.sh`, and `test-functional-ui-serial.sh` all go through that shared helper, so they stop picking your currently booted personal simulator.
- [miataru/scripts/test-screenshots.sh](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/scripts/test-screenshots.sh:10) now prefixes screenshot simulators with `miataru Screenshots - ...`, so screenshot runs use separate devices too.

miataru Tests - iPhone 16
UDID: 31221CC1-917C-43A6-AE52-DC6D6A2256F7

What you need to do now:

Run tests the same way as before:

```bash
./miataru/scripts/test-ui.sh
```

or:

```bash
./miataru/scripts/test-functional-ui-serial.sh
```

Those will now use the dedicated `miataru Tests - iPhone 16` simulator automatically.

If you want a perfectly clean test simulator before a run:

```bash
xcrun simctl shutdown "miataru Tests - iPhone 16" || true
xcrun simctl erase "miataru Tests - iPhone 16"
./miataru/scripts/test-ui.sh
```

If you run tests from Xcode with Cmd-U, Xcode still uses the simulator selected in the toolbar. For that path, manually select `miataru Tests - iPhone 16` as the run destination. The script changes protect the terminal/script workflow; Xcode’s UI destination is chosen by Xcode itself.
